clue.text: Notably soft wood for a pipe-man

parts.note: in musical notation, the mark p (piano) tells the player to go soft
lumber is cut timber

explanation.surface: A woodworker choosing a soft timber to carve a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notably' points at musical notes: soft written on a score is p. The pipe-man works on water pipes, not tobacco pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits and mends water pipes is a pipe-man.

clue.text: Bound by a solemn promise

parts.note: the whole clue describes having given one's word formally, as in a vow

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has sworn a vow is held by it, having given their word.

clue.text: Curious.1 rivals rattle you, coming' from beyond the blue

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so these letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Competitors unsettle someone with something arriving from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges RIVALS RATTLE YOU, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This radiation reaches Earth from the sun, beyond the blue sky.

clue.text: Fire and water in North Britain

explanation.surface: Flames and a Scottish stream side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a small stream is a burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on fire is to be ablaze; in Scotland a small brook is called by the same word.

clue.text: Move to accommodate female — turning up on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for female is read from bottom to top

parts.note: her is a female pronoun
the Ouse is a common English river name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A woman is moved upriver to find a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads the pronoun bottom to top in this down entry; the Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone new lodgings is to move them into accommodation.

clue.text: First-class city.

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is old slang for excellent, and a nation's seat of government is its chief city.

clue.text: By way of taking pains about rich food

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for pains goes round the other piece

parts.note: to take pains is to take care
via means by way of

explanation.surface: A cook taking great trouble over a luxurious dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... about' means the word for pains goes round 'by way of'; caviare is an older spelling of caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is an expensive delicacy, a luxurious food.

clue.text: Not ruddy poet's sphere of activity

explanation.surface: A pallid poet confined to a narrow field.
explanation.walkthrough: A pale is a fence or enclosure, hence a bounded area of action, as in 'beyond the pale'; the poetic flavour is the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: A wan face lacks colour; an enclosure or bounded district marks out the limits of what one may do.

clue.text: Go unrecognised

parts.note: go is read as make a journey, done while nobody knows who you are

explanation.definitionFit: Journeying under an assumed identity means nobody knows who you are.

clue.text: Heavyweight at full stretch?

parts.note: a large unit of weight is pictured as a heavyweight extended to its greatest length

explanation.definitionFit: The imperial weight of 2240 pounds is the larger of the two tons, the long one.

clue.text: -Melodramatic announcement once hissed from, the gallery

definitions.text: Melodramatic announcement once hissed from, the gallery

parts.words: Melodramatic announcement once hissed from, the gallery
parts.note: Victorian melodrama audiences booed and hissed the bad man as he came on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction bringing on the wicked character of a Victorian melodrama, whom the cheap seats would hiss.

clue.text: Grand service made to count in Germany

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the British armed services

explanation.surface: A fine church service held to honour a German nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Graf is the German title equal to count.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German noble title equivalent to an earl or count.

clue.text: But grease can also be extracted from this plant

indicators.note: extracted means drawn out and reworked, so these letters are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Besides sugar, a crop can also yield grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted' rearranges BUT GREASE, nine letters; 'can also be' and 'from' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A root crop grown in Europe for refining into table sweetener.

clue.text: See 11
Openly too proud to take lodgers

explanation.surface: A landlady too haughty to let rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: someone above board would think themselves too grand to give lodgers bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest dealing is done in plain view; and someone too lofty for taking in paying guests is above providing their meals.

clue.text: See 13
Trick v movement ' babies can do

explanation.surface: A tricky motion that infants manage.
explanation.walkthrough: A footballer's run with the ball is one sense; babies letting saliva trickle is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer's close control past defenders is one sense; letting saliva run from the mouth, as infants do, is the other.

clue.text: Minor planet with an electronic tail wearing away

parts.note: Eros is a well-known asteroid, a minor planet
an ion is an electrically charged particle; comets have ion tails

explanation.surface: An asteroid trailing a charged tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual loss of rock or soil by wind and water is a wearing away.

clue.text: Tedious business enough to make a friend swear

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to declare or swear

explanation.surface: A dull chore so exasperating that a companion curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear' looks like cursing; here it means to state solemnly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and long-winded bother is a tiresome affair.

clue.text: Bearing of a holy man between two rivers

indicators.note: between means set in the middle of the two river names

parts.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
St is short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A saint's dignified carriage as he stands between two streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a direction or a burden; here it is how you carry yourself. The Po is in Italy, the Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing here is how one holds the body, one's carriage or stance.

clue.text: In poor health, the jaywalker is likely to be

definitions.text: the jaywalker is likely to be

explanation.surface: A careless pedestrian ends up ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A jaywalker crosses the road carelessly and so risks being struck by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out and unwell is one sense; being knocked over by a vehicle is the other.

clue.text: Where a Frenchman introduces rococo style

indicators.note: introduces means comes first, leading in the other piece

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman

indicators.note: style here means a fashioning, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A French designer bringing the rococo look to a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' puts M first; 'style' reworks ROCOCO into OROCCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare 'Where' asks for a place, here a North African kingdom.

clue.text: As times change for a leader of Fauvism

indicators.note: change means alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art movement's leader adapting as fashions shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' reworks AS TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: The French painter Henri was a founding figure of the Fauve art movement.

clue.text: Leftover fitting freakish fellows to a T

parts.note: odd means strange or freakish
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Peculiar men fit a scrap of cloth perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' supplies its letter as written; 'fitting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant piece left after the rest is used.

clue.text: Plot, it appears, in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in means placed within the letters for the region

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties round London, in the South East (SE) of England

explanation.surface: A building plot found in the London commuter belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties surround London in south-east England, giving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land for building is a location for it.

clue.text: Accord demonstrated by 26

parts.note: agreement of the kind shown when everyone picks the same option, as in the entry at 26

explanation.definitionFit: Complete agreement or oneness is accord.

clue.text: Grew old and managed without him

indicators.note: without means the word for him is taken away

parts.note: him refers to a male, a man

explanation.surface: Someone who aged and coped alone after he left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes MAN out of MANAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older.

clue.text: Decent sort, he could start panic when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order
start means the opening letter of the word could

explanation.surface: A good fellow who might set off alarm if he is troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' gives C from 'could'; 'when upset' rearranges HE, C and PANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent sort is a pleasant, good-hearted fellow.

clue.text: See 24
It's all for one and one for all

definitions.text: It's all for one and one for all

parts.words: It's all for one and one for all
parts.note: the musketeers' motto is read as everyone voting for one option, which all share

explanation.definitionFit: A selection made with everyone in agreement, every vote going to a single option.

clue.text: Sculptor out of step with one in Berlin

indicators.note: out of step means out of order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: ein is German for one

explanation.surface: An artist marching out of time with a German companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges STEP into EPST; Jacob Epstein was a sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a famous twentieth-century sculptor.

clue.text: Capitalise on an achievement

explanation.surface: Making the most of a success.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something to advantage is one sense; a daring feat is the other.
